chapter: Return to Atlanta and move north
title: Model T drive north with Obie Walker, J. D. and Green
summary: Harvey stays behind; the trip to Philadelphia takes seven and a half weeks in a Model T, helping stalled cars along the way.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Excuse me. That was -- Chuckles was with you?
Yeah, just Chuckles, you see, because --

Shorty, well, he didn't -- he got to be a ladies' man, you know. He was -- very handsome kid, he was, and like old women like, you know, they liked him, you know, and he took advantage of it. He was that type of child, you see. And he didn't want to leave. So it was Chuckles and I, see.

Sure enough. It took us about seven and a half weeks to get to Philadelphia, you see, because we was always stopping. We had the worst looking car on the highway, you see. It was called a Model T, you see. But all these cars, they had like LaSalles, Pierce Arrows, Piersals, Essex, you know, and Nashes and Cadillacs and, you know, Lincolns, you know, and we would always have to be stopping and helping them with their cars, you know.

And they would -- people, you know, they would invite us to go someplace because they wanted to tip us, so happy we helped them start their car again, you know. See, them cars, you could get behind these cars, you know, and push them, you know, and get them to running rolling, you know, kind of

fast, and then the engine would catch up, you know. Then we'd get in our Model T and drive up and catch up, you know, follow them along, see if they don't break down again or something. So we made a lot of friends like that on the way up.
Yeah, just us three. This guy, Obi, and like Slim and Shorty, see.
Well, what was Obi's relationship to the music (store owners)? (inaudible)?
No, he wasn't. He was under contract to George Robey, see. He was a fight promoter, and Obi was on exclusive contract to George Robey. See, he was a heavyweight, you know, and --
So it was -- basically it was Lucille Achet's father-in-law --
-- that was taking you to New York?
